title: Email Open Rate Statistics: 2026 Benchmarks for Open Rates
summary: Review email open rate statistics and benchmarks, learn how privacy affects tracking, and discover tips to improve your email marketing results.
body_markdown:
Your email open rate tells you how often delivered emails register an open, but is your percentage a sign of strong performance or room to improve? Email open rate statistics give you a reference point, provided you know which benchmarks make a fair comparison.


Major email marketing platforms report average open rates ranging from 15% to 59%, depending on the type of email and industry. Comparing your results with a benchmark that closely aligns with the type of emails you send, as well as your[target audience](https://www.shopify.com/blog/target-audience) , can help you set realistic expectations for email marketing performance.


In this article, you’ll learn how to calculate your email open rate and compare it with benchmarks, including those that account for privacy features that can inflate results. You’ll also learn how to test subject lines, segment your audience, and manage your subscriber list to improve your rates.


## What is an email open rate?


An[email open rate](https://www.shopify.com/blog/email-open-rate) measures the percentage of successfully delivered emails that recipients open. The rate is calculated using unique opens, which count each recipient only once, even if they open the same email multiple times.


To calculate this rate, divide the number of unique opens by the total number of emails successfully delivered, then multiply by 100 to get a percentage. Use delivered emails rather than emails sent, since messages that[bounce](https://www.shopify.com/blog/hard-bounce-vs-soft-bounce) never reach the recipient and shouldn’t count toward your open rate.


## What is a good email open rate?


A good email open rate is generally between 20% and 22%,[according to Shopify data](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/analyze-marketing/shopify-email-analytics) , but industry benchmarks vary, making it difficult to apply as a one-size-fits-all metric. It is also important to note that, due to recent privacy changes, email open rates paint a limited picture of marketing success.


In 2021,[Apple Mail Privacy Protection](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/mail-privacy-protection/) launched as a way to prevent email senders from tracking recipients’ activity. Apple MPP preloads email content and tracking pixels, which registers emails as being opened before recipients have actually clicked to open them. This makes it more difficult for businesses to get an accurate read on their email performance and can skew open rates higher than they actually are.


The type of email also contributes significantly to its open rate:[Automated flow emails](https://www.shopify.com/blog/57720581-7-automated-email-campaigns-that-win-customers-and-keep-them-coming-back) are sent in response to specific triggers, such as a purchase, an abandoned cart, or a request for a back-in-stock notification, and they tend to have higher open rates.[Campaign emails](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/create-marketing/shopify-messaging/email/create-email) , by contrast, are marketing messages created for a selected subscriber audience, such as newsletters, sale announcements, and product launches; they tend to have lower open rates.


## Email open rate statistics and benchmarks


The following benchmarks show email open rates reported by a variety of email marketing providers and research sources:


[MailerLite’s 2026 benchmarks](https://www.mailerlite.com/blog/compare-your-email-performance-metrics-industry-benchmarks) show a median open rate of 43.46% across more than 3.6 million campaigns sent between December 2024 and November 2025 across industries. Its ecommerce-specific campaign open rate benchmark is 32.67%, but MailerLite cautions that this includes automated opens generated by Apple Mail Privacy Protection, meaning actual human open rates are lower.


[Brevo’s 2026 benchmarks](https://www.brevo.com/blog/email-marketing-benchmarks/) , based on data from more than 175,000 active customers during 2025, found an average campaign open rate of 20.73% when excluding Apple MPP bot-triggered opens, compared with 33.87% when including them. Its ecommerce benchmark was 15.50%, excluding MPP-generated opens and 30.02% including them, illustrating how the measurement method can substantially change the reported rate.


[Stripo’s 2026 research](https://research.stripo.email/b2b-email-open-rate-benchmarks-2026) is a synthesis of data from 26 sources, focusing primarily on B2B companies. It estimates a typical B2B campaign email open-rate range of 15% to 25% after filtering out Apple MPP-generated opens.


For sources that don’t exclude Apple MPP opens, open rate percentages hover around 30%, with higher rates for automated flow emails and lower rates for campaign emails.


Drawing on data from more than 183,000 customers,[Klaviyo’s 2026 Email Marketing Benchmarks](https://www.klaviyo.com/products/email-marketing/benchmarks) list open-rate benchmarks of 31% for email marketing campaigns and 32.2% for automated flow emails.[Omnisend](https://www.omnisend.com/blog/email-marketing-benchmarks/) ’s 2026 benchmarks put the average campaign open rate at 30.22%, compared with 35.53% for automated welcome emails, 37.12% for[abandoned cart emails](https://www.shopify.com/blog/abandoned-cart-emails) , and 58.80% for back-in-stock notifications.

## Tips for improving your email open rate


- Create customer segments
- Optimize subject lines
- Track and assess email performance
- Periodically clean your email list


Here are a few tips for increasing your email open rate and better connecting with subscribers:


### Create customer segments


Use[customer segmentation](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-customer-segmentation) to tailor your emails to different consumer types. Group customers into segments based on shared characteristics, such as[customer journey](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-journey-map) stage, purchase history, product preferences, website behavior, and email engagement, as well as attributes like age, gender, and location.


You can then use these segments to tailor your messaging to niche audience groups, boosting your open rate by matching your campaign objective with the appropriate audience.


### Optimize subject lines


Use concise and compelling[subject lines](https://www.shopify.com/blog/email-hooks) to capture your customer's attention. Include preview text that complements your subject line so that viewers have a better understanding of what your email is about.


When formulating your subject lines, run[A/B tests](https://www.shopify.com/blog/the-complete-guide-to-ab-testing?term=&adid=803650316523&campaignid=19683492884&utm_medium=cpc&utm_source=google&matchtype=&network=g&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=19683492884&gbraid=0AAAAADp4t0phsEh-w-Pa6Pi_vDk8u9Whv&gclid=CjwKCAjwlY3WBhANEiwApsNrLVDdIkpI2NJETJisCosJmpI62kjNYs9B-SWBG2d1v4FdZRAGMPfpQxoCR5IQAvD_BwE) using your strongest options and a small sample of subscribers. After using tests to narrow things down, use your highest-performing subject lines in your send for the rest of your audience.


### Track and assess holistic email performance


Email marketing software like[Shopify Messaging](https://www.shopify.com/email-marketing) provides[email analytics](https://www.shopify.com/analytics) to help you see how well your messaging is reaching customers and improve KPIs like open rate. Review your open rate alongside your[click-through rate](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ctr-meaning) , click-to-open rate, and[conversion rate](https://www.shopify.com/blog/email-conversion-rate) after each campaign. These metrics show how many recipients opened your message, clicked a link within it, and completed a desired action.


Avoid treating opens alone as proof of engagement. Apple’s Mail Privacy Protection can load email images automatically, registering an open, even when the recipient hasn’t read the message. Clicks and conversions provide more concrete evidence that subscribers are interacting with your content and taking action.


### Periodically clean your email list


Prioritize targeted email campaigns and remove inactive subscribers from your send lists. This will help with the[deliverability](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/create-marketing/shopify-messaging/delivery) of your emails. If you have lower open rates due to poorly targeted messaging, email service providers are more likely to filter out your messages as spam.


Although Apple MPP can lead to your open rates skewing high, you’re still able to see what percentage of your subscribers are definitely not opening your messages. This can help you identify who those customers are and determine whether you want to send a personalized message to help them reengage or drop them from your mailing list.


Create a segment of customers who are rarely opening your emails. Doing so enables you to reach out to these customers with[win-back campaigns](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/running-winback-campaigns) or remove them from your lists if they prove unresponsive, while allowing you to better target customers who are engaged and interested. Turning on the[Smart delivery](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/create-marketing/shopify-messaging/delivery#:~:text=the%20Delivery%20section%3A-,Smart%20delivery%3A,-Filters%20your%20campaign) feature in Shopify Messaging automatically filters your audience so that emails are sent only to engaged subscribers.


## Email open rate statistics FAQ


### Is a 25% email open rate good?


Yes, while open rates vary by industry and email type, a 25% email open rate is good. Brevo, for example, found an average marketing email open rate of 20.73%. It was 15.5% for ecommerce, while Stripo estimates 15% to 25% for B2C companies.


### What are the typical email open rates by industry?


The average email open rate for retail is around 27%, with ecommerce reporting a rate of about 24%. For B2B businesses, the average email open rate is roughly 20%. These rates are combined averages from different reports, and it can be difficult to find a variety of sources that compare the same exact businesses from the same exact industries.


### How do you find the open rate of an email?


The formula for calculating an email open rate is: Unique opens / total number of emails delivered x 100 (to get a percentage). Unique opens are to the number of times a new recipient opens the email. This is distinct from total opens, which includes instances in which the same recipient opens an email multiple times.
